result.executive_verdict: The state/evidence/authority skeleton (immutable Git-blob-bound evidence, conformance derived only from committed HEAD, fail-closed dispatch, runtime evidence as first-class validation) is genuinely sound and is the correct fix for the prior review's 8/8 finding. But the architecture as it exists today is not merely "sound but unbuilt" -- it contains verified, concrete defects in work already committed: at least 13 of 37 task contracts reference a Unity scene path that no longer exists, meaning the one mechanism meant to prevent concurrent scene conflicts is already desynchronized; NSC-003, the designated real-work anchor, has its persisted contract asserting decomposition_state: concrete / execution_scope: single_agent while prose documentation says it is blocked on unresolved human design questions -- a live recurrence of the exact graph-truth-vs-reality mismatch Phase 1-3 was built to eliminate; GDD-drift detection only exists for the one task that already has an evidence record, leaving 36 of 37 contracts with zero signal if the (explicitly iterating) GDD changes underneath them; and project documentation (Pipeline/Reconciliation/README.md) promises a reconciliation diff/apply workflow that does not exist anywhere in taskcontrol.py (verified directly: no diff/apply subcommands exist). Layered on top of this, three consecutive post-Milestone-1 work sessions produced zero repository-write capability and zero gameplay throughput; the only production consumer of the new AgentRuntime is the ArchitectureReview tool reviewing itself, about to run a second full 8-reviewer cycle without the corrected architecture ever having touched the game once. This is a sound design with real, fixable defects in its current instantiation, sequenced in the wrong order relative to the project's own stated rule to advance the game rather than build infrastructure indefinitely.
preserve: Task-contract schema 2.0 removing mutable status/complete/ready fields; Tasks/*.yaml is approved definition, not completion truth.

Immutable, Git-blob-SHA-bound delivery/baseline/revalidation evidence records under Pipeline/TaskGraph/evidence/, read only from committed HEAD -- demonstrated working (NSC-023 flipped not_delivered to conformant only after commit).
Deterministic current_conformance.py as the sole derivation of state; provider/agent claims remain non-authoritative until independently checked.
Fail-closed dispatch: taskcontrol ready = UNAVAILABLE, authorize = DENIED, by explicit policy rather than by omission.
GER lesson set (ADR-015 runtime evidence as first-class validation, ADR-016 no-op refinement counts as failed progress) -- both trace to the real Assignment 6 camera failure, not hypotheticals.

Reconciliation as an immutable point-in-time snapshot that never directly mutates the living graph; a review/diff/apply boundary is the right concept even though the apply tool itself does not yet exist.
Human authority retained at every real gate: Play Mode approval, PR merge, bootstrap/verification approval, dispatch-policy approval.

Unity-specific discipline: code-driven idempotent scene builder instead of hand-edited scene YAML, non-saving in-memory test seam, byte-identity assertions around committed-scene tests, and a clean-repo test runner that fails on any HEAD/tree drift.
Deterministic supervisor / bounded, replaceable LLM worker division of labor as the general control-loop shape.
change_or_replace: Fix the verified stale unity-scene exclusive_resources paths across at least 13 (unity reviewer claims 16) of 37 task contracts, and add a deterministic taskcontrol validator check that resource/evidence paths currently exist in the tree.

Resolve the NSC-003 graph-truth-vs-prose mismatch: either correct decomposition_state/execution_scope to reflect its actual blocked status, or route its open design questions through a tracked, reviewable artifact instead of an ad hoc markdown list -- do not leave the persisted graph asserting 'ready' while documentation says otherwise.
Either build a minimal reconciliation diff/apply tool or correct Pipeline/Reconciliation/README.md, which currently documents a capability that does not exist in taskcontrol.py.

Extend GDD-drift detection to open (not-yet-evidenced) task contracts, not only tasks that already have an evidence record; even a coarse per-task 'has the cited GDD section changed' check beats the current zero signal for 36 of 37 tasks.
Replace ad hoc hand-authored evidence-record JSON with a minimal authoring helper that computes Git blob SHAs, since this cost will recur on every future delivered task.

Port the already-proven Assignment 6 GER shape (generate -> deterministic/Unity evaluate -> runtime feedback -> refine -> circuit breaker) into the AgentRuntime/TaskExecution stack before or alongside any write capability, so a write-capable worker does not ship with a weaker quality gate than the earlier prototype already had.
defer_or_delete: Milestone 2's bundled RAG/Scanner/Progressive-Decomposer/Artifact-Authority platform -- no real ticket has yet hit a genuine missing-design wall that requires it.
Further OpenAI/Codex write-capability parity or a Claude-vs-Codex comparison/dual-provider launcher, until one provider has a proven write-and-merge path.

A third (or further) full 8-reviewer + synthesis + adversarial-critique ArchitectureReview cycle -- the corrected architecture has not yet touched the game once; do not spend another multi-day meta-review cycle before that happens.

Supervisor, Git worktree/claims/Draft-PR automation, dependency-derived taskcontrol ready, dispatch authorization, and any parallel-worker orchestration -- correctly still absent; the discovered stale-resource-path bug is a concrete reason concurrency must wait.

Further provider-trust-boundary adversarial hardening in AgentRuntime beyond what already exists -- the project's own ADR-038 frames this as a trusted single-user boundary; additional hardening here is not the bottleneck.

Continued standing investment in the multi-model Reconciliation Verification Crew as routine infrastructure -- keep it available for rare large-scale events, but do not extend it further after a single successful bootstrap use.

major_disagreements.issue: Overall severity: 5 of 8 reviewers labeled the architecture partially_unsound; 3 (autonomous_agent_architect, adversarial_qa, llm_reliability_engineer) labeled it sound_overbuilt, arguing the problems are purely sequencing/proportion, not soundness defects.
positions: partially_unsound camp: points to concrete, already-committed defects (stale resource paths, NSC-003 graph/prose mismatch, a documented-but-nonexistent reconciliation tool, GDD drift blind spot for 36/37 tasks) as evidence something is actually wrong, not merely unbuilt.

sound_overbuilt camp: argues the core loop shape is coherent and nothing found is a structural dead end; the real issue is that huge effort went into governance/transport machinery before the one blocking capability (write) was built, which is a build-order problem, not a design flaw.
major_disagreements.assessment: Independent verification confirms the concrete defects are real (grep-confirmed stale paths in 13 files, grep-confirmed absence of diff/apply commands, confirmed whole-file GDD hash). These are not merely 'unbuilt features' -- they are latent bugs and a documentation/implementation mismatch in already-shipped work, which tips the classification toward partially_unsound rather than purely sound-but-late. The sound_overbuilt camp's core claim about sequencing/proportion is also correct and folded into the throughput and change_or_replace findings.

major_disagreements.issue: Whether the next real-work slice should go through a human using Claude Code interactively outside AgentRuntime (fast, uses only already-built evidence tooling, no new infrastructure) or through a newly built, narrowly-scoped repository_write capability inside AgentRuntime/TaskExecution.
positions: Interactive/manual camp (unity_production_engineer, adversarial_qa, yagni_complexity_critic): implement the next small ticket directly with Claude Code as a human-supervised assistant, proving the evidence/conformance model generalizes to a second task without building new capability first.

Write-capability camp (workflow_systems_architect, autonomous_agent_architect, llm_reliability_engineer, game_technical_director, game_producer): the single biggest untested claim in the whole architecture is whether AgentRuntime itself can safely write scoped code; nothing else matters until that specific capability is proven once.
major_disagreements.assessment: The manual path is cheaper and lower-risk but would repeat exactly the pattern reviewers criticize about NSC-023 (a human-produced feature retrofitted with evidence, not a demonstration that the pipeline itself creates leverage). The narrow write-capability path is the higher-value experiment because it is the one thing every reviewer independently names as the actual bottleneck; recommended as the next slice below, scoped tightly enough that its cost is proportionate.

major_disagreements.issue: Whether the AgentInvocationRequest/TaskExecutionRequest separation (ADR-039) is correctly scoped now or built one layer too early.
positions: workflow_systems_architect treats the boundary as the correct design even though currently thin.

game_technical_director, game_producer, and autonomous_agent_architect call it premature generalization for hypothetical future consumers (ExecutionCrew, Reconciliation) that do not yet exist, evidenced by TaskExecutionRunner being a 39-line pass-through wrapper (independently confirmed by reading the file).
major_disagreements.assessment: The abstraction is cheap and already built, so ripping it out is not warranted; but it should not receive further generalization investment until it has a second real consumer beyond ArchitectureReview.

result.gdd_iteration_strategy: Reconciliation's core design (immutable snapshot, never directly mutating the living graph, requiring a review/diff/apply boundary before any graph change) is the right shape for an iterating GDD, but its implementation is currently binary and incomplete: either run the full multi-model Verification Crew (correctly reserved for bootstrap/major events) or do nothing, with no built middle tier. Verified directly: current_conformance.py only checks GDD-canon-hash drift inside the per-record evaluation loop, so the 36 of 37 task contracts without an evidence record get zero signal when the GDD changes underneath them; and the one drift check that does exist hashes the entire canonical GDD file rather than the section a task actually cites, so any edit anywhere would eventually over-trigger revalidation once more tasks carry evidence. Separately, Pipeline/Reconciliation/README.md documents a "taskcontrol reconciliation-diff/apply workflow" that does not exist in taskcontrol.py (confirmed by direct inspection: no diff or apply subcommands). The recommended strategy is: (1) correct the documentation-vs-implementation gap immediately (either build a minimal version or stop claiming it exists); (2) add a lightweight, deterministic mechanism that flags which open task contracts cite a GDD section that has since changed, even a simple section-anchor or line-range comparison, so drift is visible before a human happens to notice; (3) defer refining the whole-file-hash granularity problem until at least 2-3 tasks carry evidence records and the over-invalidation cost is actually observed, since only one task (NSC-023) has evidence today.
result.minimum_viable_architecture: Keep the four-layer state model: Tasks/*.yaml (approved definition) -> immutable Git-blob-bound evidence records -> deterministically derived current_conformance -> explicit fail-closed execution_authority gate. Keep GER's runtime-evidence and no-op-refinement rules, human merge/approval gates, and the Unity-specific test/scene-builder discipline. Cut everything downstream of a single provider's write path: do not maintain dual-provider (Claude+Codex) parity beyond read-only ArchitectureReview use until one provider has shipped one real ticket; do not build Milestone 2's RAG/Decomposer/Artifact-Authority bundle; do not extend the multi-model Reconciliation Verification Crew beyond its proven one-time bootstrap use; do not add further provider-trust-boundary hardening. The minimum viable next increment is a single narrowly-scoped repository_write capability plus a ported GER loop, exercised on one small task -- everything else in the current target architecture (supervisor, worktrees, continuous autonomy, Progressive Decomposer, provider comparison) should remain deferred until that one write-capable loop has actually shipped and been measured.

recommended_next_slice.title: Fix the verified resource-path defect, then prove one real write-capable ticket end-to-end through AgentRuntime/TaskExecution using the existing evidence model and the ported Assignment 6 GER loop
recommended_next_slice.why: Every reviewer, from multiple independent angles (workflow architecture, autonomous-agent design, LLM reliability, technical direction, production throughput), converges on the same missing capability: no provider can currently write a single file, so the entire evidence/conformance/authority apparatus has never been exercised on real work, and the pipeline's central leverage claim remains unfalsified. Before that, the newly verified stale exclusive_resources defect must be fixed, since it corrupts the exact mechanism a write-capable worker would need to rely on to avoid touching the wrong Unity assets, and the NSC-003 graph/prose mismatch must not be allowed to silently authorize a worker onto a task that is not actually ready.
deliverables: Correct all stale unity-scene exclusive_resources paths in Tasks/*.yaml to the current Assets/Scenes/DoorPrototype.unity, and add a deterministic taskcontrol validate check that resource/evidence paths exist in the current tree.

Select the smallest ready task with no open human design questions (not NSC-003, which is explicitly blocked pending human resolution of input-ownership/arbitration questions) -- reviewer-identified candidates include NSC-037 and NSC-024, subject to human confirmation they are genuinely unambiguous.

Add a narrow repository_write capability to ClaudeCodeProvider, scoped to that task's declared exclusive_resources/allowed_paths, invoked only inside a disposable Git branch/worktree (never the trusted read-only root used for ArchitectureReview), with a deterministic post-invocation Git diff-scope check rejecting any commit touching paths outside the allowlist.

Port the existing Assignment 6 GER shape (evaluate -> Unity/runtime feedback -> refine -> circuit breaker, no-op refinement counted as failed progress) into TaskExecutionRunner rather than inventing a new evaluator.
Keep dispatch manual and merge human-gated; do not change taskcontrol ready/authorize policy as part of this slice.
Produce a genuine (non-baseline) Phase 3 delivery evidence record for this task through the pipeline itself.
recommended_next_slice.success_test: taskcontrol state for the selected task derives conformant via a real delivery record (not a retrofitted baseline), the implementation was produced by an actual repository_write invocation through AgentRuntime/TaskExecution (not manual human editing), the committed diff is fully confined to the task's declared allowed_paths, the existing Unity clean-test runner reports a clean repository before and after with all tests passing, and required human Play Mode approval is recorded by name -- the first time the corrected pipeline, rather than a human or a retrofitted evidence record, has produced a conformant task since Milestone 1.

result.expected_autonomy_and_throughput: Currently zero: no gameplay task has been delivered end-to-end through the corrected pipeline since Milestone 1 completed on 2026-08-21. The only conformant task (NSC-023) was built through the earlier Assignment 6 coursework loop and later retrofitted with Phase 3A evidence records -- it is not evidence the new AgentRuntime/TaskExecution/evidence stack accelerates anything. All measured engineering effort in the observed window went into schema migration, evidence/conformance infrastructure, and dual-provider transport plumbing whose only production consumer is the ArchitectureReview tool reviewing itself. Readiness and dispatch authorization remain correctly fail-closed by explicit policy, so even after the recommended next slice, the system will remain human-supervised, single-ticket, and manually dispatched -- not autonomous. A successful next slice would establish the first real throughput data point (one small ticket, human-supervised, pipeline-produced), not a productivity multiplier; claims of "days instead of weeks" should remain unverified until several tickets have gone through the write-capable loop and elapsed time has actually been measured against unassisted development.
critical_risks: Verified: at least 13 of 37 task contracts reference a Unity scene path that no longer exists in exclusive_resources, meaning the mechanism meant to prevent concurrent scene conflicts is already silently desynchronized -- this must be fixed before any concurrency or write capability is introduced.

NSC-003's persisted contract state (decomposition_state: concrete, execution_scope: single_agent) contradicts prose documentation describing it as blocked on unresolved human design questions; a worker or automated dispatch policy trusting only the persisted graph could be handed unready work.

GDD-drift detection is invisible for 36 of 37 task contracts (only tasks with an existing evidence record are checked), so an iterating GDD -- the project's own explicit working assumption -- can silently invalidate acceptance criteria for most of the graph with no signal.

Pipeline/Reconciliation/README.md documents a diff/apply workflow that does not exist in taskcontrol.py (verified directly); any reliance on this documentation as an accurate description of current capability is misplaced.

If repository_write capability is added before the proven Assignment 6 GER repair loop is ported into AgentRuntime/TaskExecution, newly delivered code could ship with a weaker quality gate than the pipeline's own earlier, already-working prototype.

Continued recursive investment in ArchitectureReview self-review tooling (a second full 8-reviewer cycle already run within days, this synthesis being a further one) risks becoming a self-perpetuating meta-project that violates the project's own stated rule to advance the game rather than build infrastructure indefinitely.
result.decision_rationale: The eight reviews share strong overlapping evidence (the write-capability gap and zero-throughput finding appear independently in all eight, phrased differently but citing the same files) which the instructions correctly note is not independent proof by itself. What changes the classification from a milder "sound but late" reading to partially_unsound is direct, low-cost verification of specific, checkable claims: grepping Tasks/*.yaml confirmed the stale scene-path defect in at least 13 files; grepping taskcontrol.py confirmed no diff/apply subcommands exist despite being documented; reading current_conformance.py confirmed GDD-drift checking is scoped only to evidenced tasks and uses a whole-file hash; reading task_runner.py confirmed TaskExecutionRunner is a thin, unexercised pass-through. These are not opinions repeated by a shared model family -- they are facts about the current repository that happen to corroborate the majority verdict. Given that, the state/authority layer is not merely unproven, it contains real defects in already-committed work, which is why partially_unsound (not sound_overbuilt) is the more accurate classification, while still crediting the sound_overbuilt minority's correct point that the core loop shape itself does not need replacing -- only correction and resequencing.
evidence_gaps: The exact full list and count of task contracts with stale exclusive_resources paths was not exhaustively enumerated beyond one exact-string grep (13 files matched); the unity_production_engineer review claims 16 including a field in NSC-023's bootstrap evidence, which may use different quoting or may be a field that reviewer argues is intentionally historical -- a full audit of all 37 contracts was not performed here.
Whether NSC-037 or NSC-024 (reviewer-suggested candidates for the next write-capable slice) are genuinely free of open design questions was not independently confirmed by reading those task files.

The real wall-clock/human-effort cost behind the compressed 2026-08-21 to 2026-08-23 commit-date window is unknown; several reviewers flag this as materially affecting how urgently the infrastructure-before-gameplay pattern needs correcting.

No independent, non-LLM verification exists for this synthesis itself; it is subject to the same shared-provider-bias caveat the reviewers were warned about, and only Claude-provider reviews from this run were read per task scope (Codex-provider reviews and prior-run reviews were intentionally excluded).
